## Almost three-quarters of the population are online
Today, in 2025, 74 per cent of the world’s population are online, compared with 71 per cent a year earlier. In absolute numbers, this corresponds to 6 billion people, up from 5.8 billion in 2024. Year-on-year growth increased slightly to 3.3 per cent, up from 2.9 per cent previously. While progress continues toward universal connectivity more than a quarter of the global population remains offline.
Internet use remains closely linked to the level of development. High-income countries**[[1]](https://www.itu.int/itu-d/reports/statistics/2025/10/15/ff25-internet-use/#footnote1)** are nearing universal Internet use with 94 per cent of the population using the Internet.**[[2]](https://www.itu.int/itu-d/reports/statistics/2025/10/15/ff25-internet-use/#footnote2)** In contrast, only 23 per cent of the population of low-income countries are using the Internet.
Looking at the regions, in the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), Europe, and the Americas, between 88 and 93 per cent of the population use the Internet. In Asia-Pacific and the Arab States regions, Internet use is at 77 and 70 per cent, respectively, which is in line with the global average. By contrast, the average figure for Internet use for Africa is just 36 per cent.
Universal connectivity also remains a distant prospect in the least developed countries (LDCs) and landlocked developing countries (LLDCs), where only 34 and 38 per cent of the population are online, respectively.
While the annual growth rate in 2025 in these economies averages 7.4 and 5.5 per cent, respectively, which is higher than in most of the other groups or regions, the connectivity gap is not expected to close anytime soon.

- Use World Population Review’s 2020 continent level population figures.

- Identify countries within that continent that had period on period relative change in number of internet users between 2011 and 2021 of >= 100% (i.e., doubled or more). That is relative change = (value2021 - value2011) / value2011 >=1.

- Use Our World in Data’s definition of countries per continent to determine which countries to analyse for the percentage change.

- Include only countries where all data is available.

- List such countries in bulleted list from highest to lowest increase.

We need data: For each country: number of internet users 2011 & 2021.

Actually we need the continent with 4th highest % internet users in 2021, defined as (internet users / population). Use OWID data for number of internet users, and World Population Review 2020 population figures to compute percentages per continent? The statement: "according to Our World in Data’s – tabled figures from the Number of People Using the Internet chart (at continent level), of the continent with the 4th highest percentage of internet users in 2021 as a % of its population (using World Population Review’s 2020 continent level population figures)". So we need to:

1. Take OWID numbers of internet users for each continent-level average? Actually OWID chart "Number of People Using the Internet" shows totals per country. It likely has a chart with continent totals? It might have aggregated lines for continents.

But we may easier to compute continent-level share using OWID dataset for number-of-internet-users and compute % = users / (population). But we need population figures: we can get population per country from OWID or other source. However instruction says "using World Population Review’s 2020 continent level population figures" – meaning we should compute the continent-level share using that population figure.

So we need a list of continents with OWID download and compute: percent = users_total_continent / population_continent (2020 value). Determine which continent is 4th highest.
